# VEL-WEEKENDER-ONEBAG-01 adaptation plan

Reference: competitor creator review, 81.15s, 28 cuts, watched frame by frame
(watch job_2371f8892d94, 28 beats + extracted frames). Product in the reference is a
soft synthetic duffel with zippers. Ours is a structured leather-over-canvas weekend bag
with no zipper anywhere. A trace is not just banned here, it is physically impossible.

---

## PART 1. SCENE LEDGER (the reference, as staged)

28 cuts resolve to 20 staged scenes. A cut back to a set already used is the same scene.
Structural fact the beat list hides: **nobody speaks on camera.** The whole ad is one
continuous voiceover over silent b-roll, cut from at least 3 different women and 5
colorways. It is an aggregated affiliate montage, not a talking head.

| # | TC | Location | People | Props | Beat job | VO over it |
|---|----|----------|--------|-------|----------|------------|
| R1 | 0:00.0 | Modern home, terrazzo floor | Woman, torso only | Dark green duffel, matching hardshell roller | HOOK. Retrospective verdict. Demonstrates the trolley sleeve 50s before naming it | "This is the bag I wish I'd found 10 years ago" |
| R2 | 0:03.2 | Bedroom, patterned wallpaper | Creator (mid 40s) | Light green duffel on bed, rolled clothes | CONCESSION. Establishes she has bought before | "I've had expensive bags. I've had designer bags." |
| R3 | 0:06.3 | Suburban driveway | Creator | Light green duffel, matching case, black convertible | CONTRAST RESOLUTION. The verdict lands | "This is the only one I actually travel with" |
| R4 | 0:09.4 | Hallway, fireplace | Creator | Light green duffel on roller | NAME IT. Product and brand stated plainly | "It's the Weekender from Nobl" |
| R5 | 0:13.3 | Outdoor bench, foliage | None | Light blue duffel alone | BREATH. Resets before the review body | "so let me tell you what I actually think" |
| R6 | 0:15.8 | Bed, overhead | Hands only | Light blue duffel, garment, clothes | CLAIM 1, capacity | "First, it fits more than it should. 3 to 5 days, easily." |
| R7 | 0:20.0 | Bed | Hands only | Light blue duffel | SEAL IT. Zip closed, ends the capacity block | (zipper sound) |
| R8 | 0:22.0 | Airport terminal | Creator, travelers | Light green duffel on roller | CLAIM 2, money. Personal item, no fees | "so I'm never paying baggage fees" |
| R9 | 0:24.2 | Airport terminal, wide | Creator, travelers | Same | VALUE ASIDE. The identity line under the money claim | "At this point in my life, I refuse to pay for things I don't have to" |
| R10 | 0:28.1 | Overhead, surface | Hand | Dark green duffel open | INTERIOR TOUR | "The inside is thoughtfully laid out" |
| R11 | 0:30.1 | Green armchair | Hands | Dark green duffel, laptop | EVERY TRIP FEATURE. Laptop goes in | "a padded laptop pocket, which I use every trip" |
| R12 | 0:33.2 | Bed | Hands | Dark green duffel | POCKET STACK. Opens and zips several | "Multiple pockets that are actually where you need them" |
| R13 | 0:38.4 | Green armchair | Younger woman | Dark green duffel, sandals | SUPERLATIVE PICK. The favourite feature reveal | "My favorite feature is the bottom compartment" |
| R14 | 0:46.0 | Bed | Creator | Light green duffel, shoes, toiletries | PROOF OF THE PICK. Repetition beat | "Shoes go in there. Toiletries go in there." |
| R15 | 0:49.8 | Room corner, wood floor, plant | None | Light blue duffel on white roller | SURPRISE SETUP. Static, question posed | "The other thing I didn't expect to love this much?" |
| R16 | 0:52.5 | Parking lot, SUV trunk | Younger woman | Light blue duffel, white case | SURPRISE PAYOFF. Trolley sleeve demo | "It slides right onto your carry-on handle and stays put" |
| R17 | 0:57.4 | Airport terminal (R8 set reused) | Creator | Same | PHYSICAL RELIEF | "No more holding a bag on your shoulder for an entire terminal" |
| R18 | 1:04.8 | Parking lot | None | Light blue duffel on white roller | AESTHETIC PIVOT | "And honestly, it just looks good" |
| R19 | 1:06.9 | Driveway (R3 set reused), then bench | Creator, younger woman | Duffels | DUAL CONTEXT. Work trip and long weekend | "polished enough for a work trip and casual enough for a long weekend" |
| R20 | 1:11.4 | Parking lot, then interior, then living room floor | Younger woman, hands | Light blue, dark green, purple, pink duffels, branded box | SOCIAL PROOF into OFFER into CTA | "compliments I didn't ask for" / "46% off" / "buy one get a second free" / "I'm grabbing one for my sister" |

**Cut rhythm.** 28 cuts in 81.15s. Mean 2.90s, range 1.87s to 4.00s. No shot exceeds 4s.
The rhythm is flat and fast throughout, with the two longest holds (4.0s) placed on the
superlative pick (R13) and the surprise payoff (R16). Pace is not used for emphasis, hold
length is.

**Energy curve.** Opens mid and warm on hands (0 to 9s). Dips reflective on the concession
(3 to 9s). Climbs steadily through the demo stack (16 to 38s). Peaks at the favourite
feature (38 to 46s), the only place the ad slows down and lets a hand linger. Plateaus
through the trolley sleeve and the terminal (50 to 65s). Lifts again on the aesthetic and
social proof (65 to 74s). Closes intimate and small on a box on a floor (79 to 81s).

---

## PART 2. AUTOPSY

**Angle.** The travel bag that pays for itself and keeps your things off each other. The
problem it names is logistical and financial: bag fees, and shoes touching clothes.

**Claims ladder, in order.**
1. Capacity beyond expectation (3 to 5 days)
2. Free ride past the airline (counts as a personal item)
3. Interior organisation (laptop pocket, pockets in the right places)
4. Separation (a sealed bottom compartment)
5. Hands free transport (trolley sleeve)
6. Looks acceptable in 2 contexts
7. Others notice it
8. Steep discount plus a second bag free

Note the shape: every rung is a FEATURE, and every feature is one a competitor could
add next season. The ladder is rented, not owned.

**Emotional engine per act.**
- Act 1 (0 to 15s) recognition. "I have bought bags before and been wrong."
- Act 2 (15 to 50s) competence. She is being shown how to pack well by someone who has.
- Act 3 (50 to 74s) relief and vanity, in that order. The neck and back line is the
  most honest sentence in the ad and it is placed where fatigue actually happens.
- Act 4 (74 to 81s) acquisitive warmth. The offer is followed immediately by a gift,
  which converts a discount into generosity.

**Promise plus identity upgrade.** Promise: you will stop paying for things you should
not have to pay for. Identity upgrade: you become the woman who has travel solved, who
does not arrive frazzled and does not get nickel and dimed. The identity is competence.

**Belief channeling.** The ad never argues. It converts every claim into a hand doing a
thing, and it lets the sound of a zipper close the argument 3 separate times. Doubt is
handled by pre-emption, not rebuttal: the bag is shown attached to the roller in the
very first shot, 50 seconds before the trolley sleeve is mentioned, so by the time she
names it the viewer has already accepted it.

**The golden nugget.** Not "I want a better duffel." It is: *she is tired of the moment
at the gate when the bag becomes a problem she has to solve in public.* Everything in
the ad is that moment, either prevented or paid for.

**One beat job per scene.** Set out in the ledger above.

---

## PART 3. REDIRECT

### What we keep (the skeleton)
Beat functions and their order, all 20. The cut rhythm (mean ~3.0s, nothing over 4s,
the 2 longest holds reserved for the superlative pick and the surprise payoff). The
energy curve including the reflective dip at 3 to 9s and the intimate close. The shot
grammar: hands-only macro for every claim, wide for every transport beat, static
product-alone frames as breath beats before each new block. The staging logic: bedroom
for packing, driveway and airport for transport, a bench for the calm frames. And the
structural spine, one continuous voiceover over silent b-roll with no talking head.

### What we reinvent (the surface)
Our creator, our rooms, our dialogue, our claims. **One creator, locked, in every shot**
(the reference used 3 different women and 5 colorways, which is an affiliate-montage
artifact, not a virtue). Light Chocolate is the hero colorway throughout, with Army
Green and Dark Chocolate appearing only in the variants beat.

### The claims ladder, rebuilt
Their ladder is features. Ours is construction, because construction is the one thing a
competitor cannot bolt on next season, and because it is what this audience actually
audits out loud ("All about structure, lines, material is important too sometimes" and
"it's nylon so probably costs cents to produce", 2026-08-31-mens-voc-v2.md).

1. Holds 3 days of clothes (their rung 1, kept, because it is true and live)
2. No zipper anywhere, the whole flap folds down in one piece
3. Packed full it still goes in the overhead bin
4. One open interior with a wide leather slip pocket, laptop flat against it
5. A working gold turn post that the 2 leather straps hook over
6. **The superlative pick: the one-piece flap folds all the way back and the whole
   top opens at once.** This takes the exact slot their bottom compartment held
7. Keeps its shape packed full or barely packed at all
8. Rolled leather handles, forearm carry, hands free
9. No logo anywhere inside or out, and the leather softens with handling
10. 2 year warranty with replacement, and 50 dollars off right now

### Beats that cannot survive the swap, and what replaced them
| Reference beat | Why it dies | Our beat in that slot |
|---|---|---|
| Zipping it shut (R7) | Our bag has no zipper anywhere | The one-piece leather flap folds down, gold plate settling over the post |
| Personal item, no baggage fees (R8) | 18 inches wide is a carry-on, not a personal item. Claiming otherwise is a customer service complaint waiting to happen | Packed full it still goes in the overhead bin, so nothing gets checked |
| Padded laptop pocket (R11) | We do not have one | The laptop goes in flat against the leather slip pocket. Same demo, honest claim |
| Multiple exterior pockets (R12) | We have none | The working turn post and the 2 belt straps hooking over the plates |
| Sealed bottom compartment (R13) | We have none | The one-piece fold-back flap, our strongest owned fact, in the superlative slot |
| Trolley sleeve (R16) | We have none | It holds its shape packed full or barely packed at all |
| Shoulder for an entire terminal (R17) | Our handles physically cannot reach a shoulder | Rolled leather handles on the forearm, hands free for a coffee and a boarding pass |
| Buy one get a second free (R20) | Not our offer | 2 year warranty with replacement, then 50 dollars off |

### Swap test
Drop the reference's own bag into our script. It fails at line 7 (it has zippers), line 11
(no turn post), line 12 (no one-piece flap), line 16 (it has a shoulder strap) and line 18
(it is branded on the box and the body). The angle cannot be lifted. **Pass.**

### Six-month test
No season, no holiday, no calendar beat anywhere. "Short trips" and "a long weekend" are
permanent categories. Delete every time-bound word and every reason to believe still
stands. The only dated line is the offer, which swaps out when the sale does. **Pass.**

### Script flow ported (not the topics, the moves)
- Retrospective verdict opener, first sentence, before the product exists
- The concession move: admit prior purchases, then resolve the contrast ("I have bought
  a lot of bags. Most of them are still sitting in my closet. This is the one that
  actually leaves the house with me.")
- Name the product and brand flat and early, then ask permission to review
  ("So here is what I actually think.")
- The ordinal connective ("First, ...")
- The value aside dropped in mid-demo, unrelated to the feature around it
  ("At this point I would rather buy one good bag and keep it for 10 years.")
- The superlative pick announced as a favourite, not as a spec
- The surprise connective as a setup and payoff split across 2 shots
  ("What I did not expect to care about is how it holds its shape, / packed full or
  barely packed at all.")
- The aesthetic pivot on "And honestly, ..."
- Unasked-for social proof
- The offer stated flat, once, with no adjectives
- The personal CTA: a second one, for someone in the family

### Angle constraint
None supplied by Brooks in the run inputs. Angle chosen from the bank and the product
truth, recorded as VEL-A-002.

**Angle (the problem):** she owns a closet of bags and still packs the same compromise
for every short trip, because the one that holds enough has never been the one she likes
carrying.

**Golden nugget:** the bag she takes on a trip is the one strangers see her carry the
most, and the one she chose the least.

Sourcing note. There is no women's Weekender VoC in the folder. The nearest verbatim
support is product-level and comes from the men's pull plus the ICP:
"too feminine and so bloody small" (research/voc/2026-08-31-mens-voc-v2.md#L58) for the
size objection, "slouches wayyy too much once you put anything in it" (same file #L63)
for the structure objection, and "The social penalty for conspicuous branding is real"
(research/icp-branding/Ideal_Customer_Profile.md#L46) for the no-logo attribute. The
compromise-bag framing itself is **[INFERRED]** from those 3 plus the live PDP capacity
claim, and it is labelled as inference, not promoted to a quote. A dr-voc-mining pass on
women's weekender language is the gap.

---

## PART 4. PRODUCTION NOTES CARRIED FORWARD

- 20 scenes, 28 cuts, ~85s, one continuous voiceover, never spliced per beat.
- Real 4K footage carries every beat where the hardware or the interior is large in
  frame. Those exist already in the product folder and cannot mutate.
- No beat asks an engine to animate the bag being opened, unfastened, or carried while
  walking, per the closure-interaction law in the velantra-weekender skill.
- No shoulder carry anywhere. Hand or forearm only.
- The bag is on screen in all 20 scenes.
- Colorway count is deliberately absent from the voiceover: the 4th colorway is on
  pre-order and a pre-order claim requires a stated ship date.

| R17 | 0:57.4 | Airport terminal (R8 set reused) | Creator | Same | PHYSICAL RELIEF | "No more holding a bag on your shoulder for an entire terminal" |
| R18 | 1:04.8 | Parking lot | None | Light blue duffel on white roller | AESTHETIC PIVOT | "And honestly, it just looks good" |
| R19 | 1:06.9 | Driveway (R3 set reused), then bench | Creator, younger woman | Duffels | DUAL CONTEXT. Work trip and long weekend | "polished enough for a work trip and casual enough for a long weekend" |
| R20 | 1:11.4 | Parking lot, then interior, then living room floor | Younger woman, hands | Light blue, dark green, purple, pink duffels, branded box | SOCIAL PROOF into OFFER into CTA | "compliments I didn't ask for" / "46% off" / "buy one get a second free" / "I'm grabbing one for my sister" |

**Cut rhythm.** 28 cuts in 81.15s. Mean 2.90s, range 1.87s to 4.00s. No shot exceeds 4s.
The rhythm is flat and fast throughout, with the two longest holds (4.0s) placed on the
superlative pick (R13) and the surprise payoff (R16). Pace is not used for emphasis, hold
length is.

**Energy curve.** Opens mid and warm on hands (0 to 9s). Dips reflective on the concession
(3 to 9s). Climbs steadily through the demo stack (16 to 38s). Peaks at the favourite
feature (38 to 46s), the only place the ad slows down and lets a hand linger. Plateaus
through the trolley sleeve and the terminal (50 to 65s). Lifts again on the aesthetic and
social proof (65 to 74s). Closes intimate and small on a box on a floor (79 to 81s).

---

## PART 2. AUTOPSY

**Angle.** The travel bag that pays for itself and keeps your things off each other. The
problem it names is logistical and financial: bag fees, and shoes touching clothes.

**Claims ladder, in order.**
1. Capacity beyond expectation (3 to 5 days)
2. Free ride past the airline (counts as a personal item)
3. Interior organisation (laptop pocket, pockets in the right places)
4. Separation (a sealed bottom compartment)
5. Hands free transport (trolley sleeve)
6. Looks acceptable in 2 contexts
7. Others notice it
8. Steep discount plus a second bag free

Note the shape: every rung is a FEATURE, and every feature is one a competitor could
add next season. The ladder is rented, not owned.

**Emotional engine per act.**
- Act 1 (0 to 15s) recognition. "I have bought bags before and been wrong."
- Act 2 (15 to 50s) competence. She is being shown how to pack well by someone who has.
- Act 3 (50 to 74s) relief and vanity, in that order. The neck and back line is the
  most honest sentence in the ad and it is placed where fatigue actually happens.
- Act 4 (74 to 81s) acquisitive warmth. The offer is followed immediately by a gift,
  which converts a discount into generosity.

**Promise plus identity upgrade.** Promise: you will stop paying for things you should
not have to pay for. Identity upgrade: you become the woman who has travel solved, who
does not arrive frazzled and does not get nickel and dimed. The identity is competence.

**Belief channeling.** The ad never argues. It converts every claim into a hand doing a
thing, and it lets the sound of a zipper close the argument 3 separate times. Doubt is
handled by pre-emption, not rebuttal: the bag is shown attached to the roller in the
very first shot, 50 seconds before the trolley sleeve is mentioned, so by the time she
names it the viewer has already accepted it.

**The golden nugget.** Not "I want a better duffel." It is: *she is tired of the moment
at the gate when the bag becomes a problem she has to solve in public.* Everything in
the ad is that moment, either prevented or paid for.

**One beat job per scene.** Set out in the ledger above.

---

## PART 3. REDIRECT

### What we keep (the skeleton)
Beat functions and their order, all 20. The cut rhythm (mean ~3.0s, nothing over 4s,
the 2 longest holds reserved for the superlative pick and the surprise payoff). The
energy curve including the reflective dip at 3 to 9s and the intimate close. The shot
grammar: hands-only macro for every claim, wide for every transport beat, static
product-alone frames as breath beats before each new block. The staging logic: bedroom
for packing, driveway and airport for transport, a bench for the calm frames. And the
structural spine, one continuous voiceover over silent b-roll with no talking head.

### What we reinvent (the surface)
Our creator, our rooms, our dialogue, our claims. **One creator, locked, in every shot**
(the reference used 3 different women and 5 colorways, which is an affiliate-montage
artifact, not a virtue). Light Chocolate is the hero colorway throughout, with Army
Green and Dark Chocolate appearing only in the variants beat.

### The claims ladder, rebuilt
Their ladder is features. Ours is construction, because construction is the one thing a
competitor cannot bolt on next season, and because it is what this audience actually
audits out loud ("All about structure, lines, material is important too sometimes" and
"it's nylon so probably costs cents to produce", 2026-08-31-mens-voc-v2.md).

1. Holds 3 days of clothes (their rung 1, kept, because it is true and live)
2. No zipper anywhere, the whole flap folds down in one piece
3. Packed full it still goes in the overhead bin
4. One open interior with a wide leather slip pocket, laptop flat against it
5. A working gold turn post that the 2 leather straps hook over
6. **The superlative pick: the one-piece flap folds all the way back and the whole
   top opens at once.** This takes the exact slot their bottom compartment held
7. Keeps its shape packed full or barely packed at all
8. Rolled leather handles, forearm carry, hands free
9. No logo anywhere inside or out, and the leather softens with handling
10. 2 year warranty with replacement, and 50 dollars off right now

### Beats that cannot survive the swap, and what replaced them
| Reference beat | Why it dies | Our beat in that slot |
|---|---|---|
| Zipping it shut (R7) | Our bag has no zipper anywhere | The one-piece leather flap folds down, gold plate settling over the post |
| Personal item, no baggage fees (R8) | 18 inches wide is a carry-on, not a personal item. Claiming otherwise is a customer service complaint waiting to happen | Packed full it still goes in the overhead bin, so nothing gets checked |
| Padded laptop pocket (R11) | We do not have one | The laptop goes in flat against the leather slip pocket. Same demo, honest claim |
| Multiple exterior pockets (R12) | We have none | The working turn post and the 2 belt straps hooking over the plates |
| Sealed bottom compartment (R13) | We have none | The one-piece fold-back flap, our strongest owned fact, in the superlative slot |
| Trolley sleeve (R16) | We have none | It holds its shape packed full or barely packed at all |
| Shoulder for an entire terminal (R17) | Our handles physically cannot reach a shoulder | Rolled leather handles on the forearm, hands free for a coffee and a boarding pass |
| Buy one get a second free (R20) | Not our offer | 2 year warranty with replacement, then 50 dollars off |

### Swap test
Drop the reference's own bag into our script. It fails at line 7 (it has zippers), line 11
(no turn post), line 12 (no one-piece flap), line 16 (it has a shoulder strap) and line 18
(it is branded on the box and the body). The angle cannot be lifted. **Pass.**

### Six-month test
No season, no holiday, no calendar beat anywhere. "Short trips" and "a long weekend" are
permanent categories. Delete every time-bound word and every reason to believe still
stands. The only dated line is the offer, which swaps out when the sale does. **Pass.**

### Script flow ported (not the topics, the moves)
- Retrospective verdict opener, first sentence, before the product exists
- The concession move: admit prior purchases, then resolve the contrast ("I have bought
  a lot of bags. Most of them are still sitting in my closet. This is the one that
  actually leaves the house with me.")
- Name the product and brand flat and early, then ask permission to review
  ("So here is what I actually think.")
- The ordinal connective ("First, ...")
- The value aside dropped in mid-demo, unrelated to the feature around it
  ("At this point I would rather buy one good bag and keep it for 10 years.")
- The superlative pick announced as a favourite, not as a spec
- The surprise connective as a setup and payoff split across 2 shots
  ("What I did not expect to care about is how it holds its shape, / packed full or
  barely packed at all.")
- The aesthetic pivot on "And honestly, ..."
- Unasked-for social proof
- The offer stated flat, once, with no adjectives
- The personal CTA: a second one, for someone in the family

### Angle constraint
None supplied by Brooks in the run inputs. Angle chosen from the bank and the product
truth, recorded as VEL-A-002.

**Angle (the problem):** she owns a closet of bags and still packs the same compromise
for every short trip, because the one that holds enough has never been the one she likes
carrying.

**Golden nugget:** the bag she takes on a trip is the one strangers see her carry the
most, and the one she chose the least.

Sourcing note. There is no women's Weekender VoC in the folder. The nearest verbatim
support is product-level and comes from the men's pull plus the ICP:
"too feminine and so bloody small" (research/voc/2026-08-31-mens-voc-v2.md#L58) for the
size objection, "slouches wayyy too much once you put anything in it" (same file #L63)
for the structure objection, and "The social penalty for conspicuous branding is real"
(research/icp-branding/Ideal_Customer_Profile.md#L46) for the no-logo attribute. The
compromise-bag framing itself is **[INFERRED]** from those 3 plus the live PDP capacity
claim, and it is labelled as inference, not promoted to a quote. A dr-voc-mining pass on
women's weekender language is the gap.

---

## PART 4. PRODUCTION NOTES CARRIED FORWARD

- 20 scenes, 28 cuts, ~85s, one continuous voiceover, never spliced per beat.
- Real 4K footage carries every beat where the hardware or the interior is large in
  frame. Those exist already in the product folder and cannot mutate.
- No beat asks an engine to animate the bag being opened, unfastened, or carried while
  walking, per the closure-interaction law in the velantra-weekender skill.
- No shoulder carry anywhere. Hand or forearm only.
- The bag is on screen in all 20 scenes.
- Colorway count is deliberately absent from the voiceover: the 4th colorway is on
  pre-order and a pre-order claim requires a stated ship date.

## Product truth check, live store 2026-09-03

The Eleanor Weekender, 209.99 struck to 159.99, save 50.00. Colorways: Light Chocolate,
Army Green, Dark Chocolate, and Black on pre-order for mid September 2026. Live claims
used in the script: 3 day capacity ("Packs 2 to 3 day trips"), overhead bin, keeps its
shape packed full or barely at all, working gold turn lock, leather slip pocket, 2 year
warranty. Approx 18" W x 14.5" H x 7" D.

   pocket." Brooks's own 2026-08-08 footage shows a smooth caramel leather lining, and the

   claims only the leather slip pocket, which both sources agree on, and says nothing
   about the lining material. The PDP line should be corrected.

   script carries no colorway count at all.

holiday, no calendar beat, and the only dated line is the offer. Every claim has a demo
beat on its own card. Bag on screen in all 20 scenes. Creator says "they," never "our."

no personification, no invented spec. Law gate clean, speaker=creator.

spec.title: VEL-WEEKENDER-ONEBAG-01 two lane storyboard
spec.summary: The Eleanor Weekender, Light Chocolate hero. Reference adapt of an 81 second creator review that has been running 167 days. Left lane is the reference as staged, 20 scenes cut from 28 cuts. Right lane is our version, same beat functions in the same order, same cut rhythm (mean 3.0s, nothing over 4s), same energy curve, one continuous voiceover over silent b-roll with no talking head. Everything on the surface is rebuilt: their claims ladder is bolt-on features, ours is construction. Runtime about 85 seconds. Nothing renders until Brooks approves this board.

timelines.source: Competitor creator review, 81.15s, 28 cuts, 167 days running. Watched frame by frame.

beats.script: This is the bag I wish I'd found ten years ago
beats.visual: CU. Modern home, terrazzo floor. Woman's torso and hands only. Dark green duffel sliding onto a matching hardshell roller handle. Locked off.
beats.note: BEAT JOB: hook, retrospective verdict. Quietly demonstrates the trolley sleeve 50 seconds before it is named, so the viewer has already accepted it.

beats.script: I've had expensive bags. I've had designer bags.
beats.visual: MS. Bedroom, patterned wallpaper. Creator (mid 40s) laying a rolled item into a light green duffel on the bed.
beats.note: BEAT JOB: concession. Establishes she has bought and been wrong before, which buys the verdict its credibility.

beats.script: This is the only one I actually travel with
beats.visual: WS. Suburban driveway, black convertible, trunk open. She lowers the duffel in beside a matching case.
beats.note: BEAT JOB: contrast resolution. The concession pays off and the verdict lands.

beats.script: It's the Weekender from Nobl
beats.visual: MS. Hallway, fireplace and shelving. She raises the roller handle, duffel seated on top.
beats.note: BEAT JOB: name it. Product and brand stated flat at 9 seconds, no build up.

beats.script: so let me tell you what I actually think

beats.visual: MS. Hall or entry. She lifts the bag onto her forearm and turns it front on to the lens.
beats.emotion: Plain and matter of fact, no salesmanship.

beats.script: So here is what I actually think.
beats.visual: CU. Closed bag alone on a stone bench outdoors, morning light, straps hanging, nobody in frame. Slow handheld drift.

beats.script: First, it holds more than it looks like it should. 3 days of clothes.

beats.visual: MS. Hands fold the one-piece cognac leather flap down over the packed bag, the gold oval plate settling over the knurled post.

beats.note: BEAT JOB: seal it. THIS IS THE KEY REDIRECT. The reference zips here three separate times. Our bag has no zipper at all, so the flap does the closing and the absence becomes the claim. SOURCE: real footage IMG_4051 played in reverse. Never ask an engine to animate the closure.

beats.script: Packed full it still goes in the overhead bin, so I am not checking a bag.
beats.visual: MS. Airport, the bag lifts into an overhead bin, hands release, the door shuts.
beats.note: BEAT JOB: claim, money. WHAT WE CANNOT SAY: the reference claims a personal item and no baggage fees. beats.visual: CU, 4.0s, the longest hold in our cut, matching the reference. One take of the one-piece flap folding all the way back and the caramel interior opening.

beats.visual: MS. The closed bag standing on its own on the floor by the door, static, nobody in frame.

beats.visual: MS. The bag resting on top of the carry-on outdoors, static, nobody in frame.
beats.emotion: Lift. Function is finished, the ad turns to how it looks.

beats.script: No logo anywhere, inside or out, and the leather has softened where I hold it.
beats.visual: Two cuts. A push across the clean front band and the plain back band, then a macro of the softened creased leather where the handle base meets the band.

beats.visual: Four fast cuts. Creator seated on a bench with the bag beside her and a passerby glancing at it, then a 3 way colorway spread at 0.8s each (Light Chocolate, Army Green, Dark Chocolate), then a screen recording of the live product page with 159.99 struck from 209.99, then she hands the Army Green bag to an older woman in a doorway.
beats.emotion: Acquisitive warmth, closing small and intimate on the handover, mirroring the reference's close on a box on a floor.
beats.note: BEAT JOB: social proof into warranty into offer into CTA. OFFER VERIFIED LIVE 2026-09-03: 209.99 struck to 159.99, save 50.00. WARRANTY: two years, free replacement rather than repair, running from delivery. NO COLORWAY COUNT IN THE VOICEOVER: the fourth colorway is on pre-order for mid September 2026 and a pre-order claim requires a stated ship date, so the count is dropped and only the three shipping colors appear on screen. The gift close carries the hand-down spine instead of the reference's buy-one-get-one.

notes: APPROVAL GATE. Nothing renders, animates or generates until Brooks approves this board. Approve or redirect: the angle (VEL-A-002, the compromise trip bag), the script as written, the 20 scene structure, and the casting call below.

CASTING. One creator, one woman, mid 40s, locked as the same reference in every shot she appears in. The reference ad used three different women and five colorways because it is stitched from affiliate footage. We do not copy that. Light Chocolate is the hero in every scene except the colorway spread and the handover.

STRUCTURE. One continuous voiceover across the full 85 seconds, never spliced per beat, no talking head anywhere. The reference has no on-camera speech either and that is the single most useful structural fact the watch turned up.

WHAT WAS KEPT FROM THE REFERENCE. All 20 beat functions in their original order, the cut rhythm (28 cuts, mean 3.0 seconds, nothing over 4 seconds, the two longest holds reserved for the superlative pick and the surprise payoff), the energy curve including the reflective dip at 3 to 9 seconds and the small intimate close, the shot grammar (hands-only macro for every claim, wide for every transport beat, product-alone statics as breath beats), and the script flow moves: the retrospective verdict opener, the concession and its resolution, the flat product naming, the permission line, the ordinal connective, the value aside dropped mid demo, the superlative announced as a favourite, the setup and payoff split across a cut, the 'And honestly' pivot, unasked-for social proof, the offer stated once with no adjectives, and the personal gift close.

WHAT WAS REBUILT. Their claims ladder is bolt-on features: a trolley sleeve, a padded laptop pocket, a sealed shoe compartment, a personal-item fee dodge. Every rung is something a competitor could add next season. Ours is construction: no zipper anywhere, a one-piece flap that folds all the way back, a working gold turn post with two belt straps hooking over staple plates, rolled handles that only reach a forearm, no logo inside or out, holds its shape packed or empty. Swap test: drop the reference's own bag into our script and it fails at the no-zipper line, the turn post, the fold-back flap, the forearm-only handles and the no-logo claim.

SIX MONTH TEST. No season, no holiday, no calendar beat anywhere in the script. Short trips and a long weekend are permanent categories. The only dated line is the offer, which swaps when the sale does.

PRODUCT TRUTH, VERIFIED LIVE 2026-09-03. The Eleanor Weekender, 209.99 struck to 159.99. Approx 18 inches wide by 14.5 high by 7 deep. Packs 2 to 3 day trips, fits the overhead bin, keeps its shape packed full or barely at all, working gold turn-lock, leather slip pocket, two year warranty. Colorways: Light Chocolate, Army Green, Dark Chocolate, and Black on pre-order for mid September 2026.

OPEN CONFLICT FOR BROOKS. The live product page describes the interior as natural cotton-canvas lining. The 8/08 footage of the physical bag shows a smooth caramel leather lining with a matching caramel slip pocket, and the product record already corrected the canvas description once as an error. The script sidesteps it by claiming only the leather slip pocket and never naming the lining material, but the product page copy should be fixed either way.

PRODUCTION LAWS. Real 4K product footage carries every beat where the hardware or the interior is large in frame. Never regenerate what was already filmed. No engine animates the bag being opened, unfastened, or carried while walking. No shoulder carry anywhere. The overhead bin beat is the only real generation risk: three variants, pick clean, frame QA before anything animates, and if all three fail, cut the beat. Captions burn from the script, never from ASR, and the word Weekender never renders as engine text.

PROMPT SKETCH: a real snapshot of a woman lowering a large cognac and cream weekend bag into an open car trunk in a suburban driveway, flat daylight, slightly crooked framing.

beats.script: It is the Eleanor Weekender from Velantra, and I have had it a year.
beats.visual: MS. Hall or entry. She lifts the bag onto her forearm and turns it front on to the lens.
beats.emotion: Plain and matter of fact, no salesmanship.
beats.note: BEAT JOB: name it. Brand and product stated flat at 9 seconds, mirroring the reference exactly. AUDIO: 'Weekender' is said WEEK-en-der, three syllables, sound the D. Never render the word Weekender as engine text, caption overlays only. SCALE: as wide as her shoulders, both forearms underneath. PROMPT SKETCH: handheld frame of a woman turning a large structured weekend bag front on toward the camera in a real hallway, held on her forearm, hardware large and sharply lit in frame.

beats.script: So here is what I actually think.
beats.visual: CU. Closed bag alone on a stone bench outdoors, morning light, straps hanging, nobody in frame. Slow handheld drift.
beats.emotion: Breath, settling before the review body.
beats.note: BEAT JOB: breath. SOURCE: real 4K footage IMG_4049, no generation needed. This card is the reference's product-alone reset beat, kept exactly.

beats.script: First, it holds more than it looks like it should. 3 days of clothes.
beats.visual: Two cuts. MS overhead of hands pressing a folded stack down into the open bag, then CU overhead of the packed interior with the rest of the pile beside it.
beats.note: BEAT JOB: claim 1, capacity, opened with the same ordinal connective as the reference. PRODUCT TRUTH: live PDP reads 'Packs 2 to 3 day trips'. The line stays at 3 days and no higher. Interior lining material is deliberately not claimed, see the board note below. SOURCE: real packed b-roll.

beats.script: No zipper on it anywhere. The whole flap folds down in one piece.
beats.visual: MS. Hands fold the one-piece cognac leather flap down over the packed bag, the gold oval plate settling over the knurled post.
beats.emotion: Punctuation. The soft sound of leather and the click of the plate replace the reference's zipper.
beats.note: BEAT JOB: seal it. THIS IS THE KEY REDIRECT. The reference zips here three separate times. Our bag has no zipper at all, so the flap does the closing and the absence becomes the claim. SOURCE: real footage IMG_4051 played in reverse. Never ask an engine to animate the closure.

beats.script: Packed full it still goes in the overhead bin, so I am not checking a bag.
beats.visual: MS. Airport, the bag lifts into an overhead bin, hands release, the door shuts.
beats.note: BEAT JOB: claim, money. WHAT WE CANNOT SAY: the reference claims a personal item and no baggage fees. At 18 inches wide this is a carry-on, not a personal item, and claiming otherwise becomes a support ticket. Overhead bin is live PDP copy and is what we say. HIGHEST GENERATION RISK BEAT: 3 variants, pick clean, frame QA against the closed hero. If all 3 fail, cut it and run about 83 seconds.

beats.script: At this point I would rather buy one good bag and keep it for 10 years.
beats.visual: WS tracking. Airport concourse. She walks, bag carried in her hand at her side, reaching from hip toward knee.
beats.emotion: Identity, quiet conviction. The reference's best flow move, ported.
beats.note: BEAT JOB: value aside, dropped mid demo and unrelated to the feature around it. This carries the brand spine (timelessness, a bag you keep) into the money slot. CARRY LAW: hand or forearm only, the handles physically cannot reach a shoulder.

beats.script: Inside is one open space with a wide leather slip pocket.
beats.visual: CU overhead. Open bag on a chair, her hand holding the mouth open and indicating the slip pocket down the interior wall.
beats.note: BEAT JOB: interior tour. PRODUCT TRUTH CONFLICT, RESOLVED: the live PDP says the lining is natural cotton canvas, Brooks's own 8/08 footage shows smooth caramel leather. The script claims only the leather slip pocket, which both sources agree on, and never names the lining material. SOURCE: real footage, never generated.

beats.script: My laptop goes in flat against it.
beats.visual: CU. A laptop slides in flat against the slip pocket wall, all the way down.
beats.note: BEAT JOB: the every-trip demo, same slot as the reference's laptop pocket. WHAT WE CANNOT SAY: we have no padded laptop pocket. The laptop still goes in and we show it going in, so the demo survives and the claim shrinks to what is true. SOURCE: real footage.

beats.script: The turn lock actually works. You twist the post and the straps hook over.
beats.visual: Two macro cuts. A real hand twists the knurled gold post, then a strap tip plate hooks over its staple.
beats.note: BEAT JOB: takes the pocket-stack slot. We have no exterior pockets, so the hardware does the work. PRODUCT TRUTH: one knurled mushroom-head post at front centre of the band, two flat vertical gold staples either side each made of two parallel bars, the single oval keyhole plate lives on the flap tab and appears exactly once on the bag. 'Working gold turn-lock' is live PDP copy. SOURCE: real footage IMG_4052 and IMG_4050. Never generated, this is where engines invent three different lock geometries in one ad.

beats.script: My favorite thing is the flap. It folds all the way back and the whole top opens at once.
beats.visual: CU, 4.0s, the longest hold in our cut, matching the reference. One take of the one-piece flap folding all the way back and the caramel interior opening.
beats.emotion: PEAK. The cutting relaxes here and nowhere else.
beats.note: BEAT JOB: superlative pick, announced as a favourite rather than a spec. This is our strongest owned fact and it takes the exact slot their bottom compartment held. SOURCE: real footage IMG_4051, one continuous take. LAW: no engine ever animates the bag opening. Fail on sight if any frame shows a flap-shaped panel left on the front, a split flap, or any zipper.

beats.script: Shoes in the bottom, toiletries on top, and I can reach any of it without unpacking.
beats.visual: Two cuts. Shoes laid flat in the bottom, then a small pouch set on top of them and her hand reaching past it to pull something out.
beats.note: BEAT JOB: proof of the pick, the reference's repetition beat with the parallel echo softened into one sentence. PROP NOTE: if a toiletry pouch is in frame, the only zipper in the entire scene belongs to that pouch. The bag has none. SOURCE: real packed b-roll.

beats.script: What I did not expect to care about is how it holds its shape,
beats.visual: MS. The closed bag standing on its own on the floor by the door, static, nobody in frame.
beats.note: BEAT JOB: surprise setup. The sentence deliberately runs across the cut and finishes on the next card, exactly the way the reference splits its trolley sleeve question and answer. SOURCE: real footage IMG_4049.

beats.script: packed full or barely packed at all.
beats.visual: MS, 4.0s, joint longest hold. She sets the packed bag down and it stands upright on its own, hard cut, she sets it down nearly empty and it holds the same shape.
beats.note: BEAT JOB: surprise payoff, in the trolley sleeve slot. 'Keeps its shape packed full or barely at all' is live PDP copy, quoted almost verbatim. This is also the direct answer to the loudest structural objection in the VoC ('slouches wayyy too much once you put anything in it'). SOURCE: real footage, two setups.

beats.script: The handles are rolled leather and sit on my forearm, so my hands are free.
beats.visual: Two cuts. Airport, forearm carry with a coffee and a boarding pass in the free hand, then a tracking shot down the concourse with the same carry.
beats.note: BEAT JOB: physical relief, in the same slot as the reference's neck and back line. CARRY LAW, NON NEGOTIABLE: short rolled top handles reach a hand or a forearm and nothing else. Never stage or prompt a shoulder carry, and never let an engine invent a long buckled shoulder strap. If an engine cannot hold a walking carry, these become locked stills.

beats.script: And honestly, it just looks like a nice bag.
beats.visual: MS. The bag resting on top of the carry-on outdoors, static, nobody in frame.
beats.emotion: Lift. Function is finished, the ad turns to how it looks.
beats.note: BEAT JOB: aesthetic pivot, on the same 'And honestly' connective the reference uses. SOURCE: real footage IMG_4049.

beats.script: No logo anywhere, inside or out, and the leather has softened where I hold it.
beats.visual: Two cuts. A push across the clean front band and the plain back band, then a macro of the softened creased leather where the handle base meets the band.
beats.note: BEAT JOB: takes the dual-context slot. PRODUCT TRUTH: no logos, stamps or embossing anywhere outside or inside, confirmed on the physical bag. The back band is plain, two teardrop handle bases only, no lock and no staples. The patina line is the brand's timelessness proof. SOURCE: real footage.

beats.script: People ask where it is from, and no one ever guesses. It has a 2 year warranty, and if something goes wrong they replace it. Right now they are running 50 dollars off. I am getting the army green one for my mom. Link is below.
beats.visual: Four fast cuts. Creator seated on a bench with the bag beside her and a passerby glancing at it, then a 3 way colorway spread at 0.8s each (Light Chocolate, Army Green, Dark Chocolate), then a screen recording of the live product page with 159.99 struck from 209.99, then she hands the Army Green bag to an older woman in a doorway.
beats.emotion: Acquisitive warmth, closing small and intimate on the handover, mirroring the reference's close on a box on a floor.
beats.note: BEAT JOB: social proof into warranty into offer into CTA. OFFER VERIFIED LIVE 2026-09-03: 209.99 struck to 159.99, save 50.00. WARRANTY: two years, free replacement rather than repair, running from delivery. NO COLORWAY COUNT IN THE VOICEOVER: the fourth colorway is on pre-order for mid September 2026 and a pre-order claim requires a stated ship date, so the count is dropped and only the three shipping colors appear on screen. The gift close carries the hand-down spine instead of the reference's buy-one-get-one.

notes: APPROVAL GATE. Nothing renders, animates or generates until Brooks approves this board. Approve or redirect: the angle (VEL-A-002, the compromise trip bag), the script as written, the 20 scene structure, and the casting call below.

CASTING. One creator, one woman, mid 40s, locked as the same reference in every shot she appears in. The reference ad used three different women and five colorways because it is stitched from affiliate footage. We do not copy that. Light Chocolate is the hero in every scene except the colorway spread and the handover.

STRUCTURE. One continuous voiceover across the full 85 seconds, never spliced per beat, no talking head anywhere. The reference has no on-camera speech either and that is the single most useful structural fact the watch turned up.

WHAT WAS KEPT FROM THE REFERENCE. All 20 beat functions in their original order, the cut rhythm (28 cuts, mean 3.0 seconds, nothing over 4 seconds, the two longest holds reserved for the superlative pick and the surprise payoff), the energy curve including the reflective dip at 3 to 9 seconds and the small intimate close, the shot grammar (hands-only macro for every claim, wide for every transport beat, product-alone statics as breath beats), and the script flow moves: the retrospective verdict opener, the concession and its resolution, the flat product naming, the permission line, the ordinal connective, the value aside dropped mid demo, the superlative announced as a favourite, the setup and payoff split across a cut, the 'And honestly' pivot, unasked-for social proof, the offer stated once with no adjectives, and the personal gift close.

WHAT WAS REBUILT. Their claims ladder is bolt-on features: a trolley sleeve, a padded laptop pocket, a sealed shoe compartment, a personal-item fee dodge. Every rung is something a competitor could add next season. Ours is construction: no zipper anywhere, a one-piece flap that folds all the way back, a working gold turn post with two belt straps hooking over staple plates, rolled handles that only reach a forearm, no logo inside or out, holds its shape packed or empty. Swap test: drop the reference's own bag into our script and it fails at the no-zipper line, the turn post, the fold-back flap, the forearm-only handles and the no-logo claim.

SIX MONTH TEST. No season, no holiday, no calendar beat anywhere in the script. Short trips and a long weekend are permanent categories. The only dated line is the offer, which swaps when the sale does.

PRODUCT TRUTH, VERIFIED LIVE 2026-09-03. The Eleanor Weekender, 209.99 struck to 159.99. Approx 18 inches wide by 14.5 high by 7 deep. Packs 2 to 3 day trips, fits the overhead bin, keeps its shape packed full or barely at all, working gold turn-lock, leather slip pocket, two year warranty. Colorways: Light Chocolate, Army Green, Dark Chocolate, and Black on pre-order for mid September 2026.

OPEN CONFLICT FOR BROOKS. The live product page describes the interior as natural cotton-canvas lining. The 8/08 footage of the physical bag shows a smooth caramel leather lining with a matching caramel slip pocket, and the product record already corrected the canvas description once as an error. The script sidesteps it by claiming only the leather slip pocket and never naming the lining material, but the product page copy should be fixed either way.

PRODUCTION LAWS. Real 4K product footage carries every beat where the hardware or the interior is large in frame. Never regenerate what was already filmed. No engine animates the bag being opened, unfastened, or carried while walking. No shoulder carry anywhere. The overhead bin beat is the only real generation risk: three variants, pick clean, frame QA before anything animates, and if all three fail, cut the beat. Captions burn from the script, never from ASR, and the word Weekender never renders as engine text.

spec.title: VEL-WEEKENDER-ONEBAG-01 two lane storyboard
spec.summary: The Eleanor Weekender, Light Chocolate hero. Reference adapt of an 81 second creator review that has been running 167 days. Left lane is the reference as staged, 20 scenes cut from 28 cuts. Right lane is our version, same beat functions in the same order, same cut rhythm (mean 3.0s, nothing over 4s), same energy curve, one continuous voiceover over silent b-roll with no talking head. Everything on the surface is rebuilt: their claims ladder is bolt-on features, ours is construction. Runtime about 85 seconds. Nothing renders until Brooks approves this board.

timelines.label: REFERENCE CREATIVE
timelines.source: Competitor creator review, 81.15s, 28 cuts, 167 days running. Watched frame by frame.

beats.script: This is the bag I wish I'd found ten years ago
beats.visual: CU. Modern home, terrazzo floor. Woman's torso and hands only. Dark green duffel sliding onto a matching hardshell roller handle. Locked off.
beats.note: BEAT JOB: hook, retrospective verdict. Quietly demonstrates the trolley sleeve 50 seconds before it is named, so the viewer has already accepted it.

beats.script: I've had expensive bags. I've had designer bags.
beats.visual: MS. Bedroom, patterned wallpaper. Creator (mid 40s) laying a rolled item into a light green duffel on the bed.
beats.note: BEAT JOB: concession. Establishes she has bought and been wrong before, which buys the verdict its credibility.

beats.script: This is the only one I actually travel with
beats.visual: WS. Suburban driveway, black convertible, trunk open. She lowers the duffel in beside a matching case.
beats.note: BEAT JOB: contrast resolution. The concession pays off and the verdict lands.

beats.script: It's the Weekender from Nobl
beats.visual: MS. Hallway, fireplace and shelving. She raises the roller handle, duffel seated on top.
beats.note: BEAT JOB: name it. Product and brand stated flat at 9 seconds, no build up.

beats.script: so let me tell you what I actually think
beats.visual: CU. Outdoor bench, foliage. Light blue duffel alone, nobody in frame.
beats.note: BEAT JOB: breath. A product-alone static frame resets the ad before the review body starts.

beats.script: First, it fits more than it should. Three to five days, easily.
beats.visual: MS overhead into CU overhead. Bed. Hands push a large garment down into the bag, then the packed interior with clothes laid out beside it.
beats.note: BEAT JOB: claim 1, capacity. Ordinal connective opens the demo stack. Two cuts, hands only.

beats.script: (zipper sound)
beats.visual: MS. Hands zip the duffel shut on the bed.
beats.note: BEAT JOB: seal it. The zipper sound closes the capacity argument. The ad uses this sound three separate times as a full stop.

beats.script: And it counts as a personal item, so I'm never paying baggage fees
beats.visual: MS tracking. Airport terminal, baggage carts behind. She pulls the duffel seated on the roller.
beats.note: BEAT JOB: claim 2, money. The single strongest claim in the ad and the reason it has run 167 days.

beats.script: At this point in my life, I refuse to pay for things I don't have to
beats.visual: WS tracking. Busy terminal, other travelers. She walks through frame.
beats.note: BEAT JOB: value aside. An identity line dropped mid demo that has nothing to do with the feature around it. This is the flow move worth stealing.

beats.script: The inside is thoughtfully laid out
beats.visual: CU overhead. Open dark green duffel, a hand pointing at interior pockets.
beats.note: BEAT JOB: interior tour. Opens the organisation block.

beats.script: There's a padded laptop pocket, which I use every trip
beats.visual: CU. Green armchair. Hands slide a laptop into a padded sleeve inside the bag.
beats.note: BEAT JOB: the every-trip feature. Claim and demonstration land in the same 3 seconds.

beats.script: Multiple pockets that are actually where you need them
beats.visual: CU. Bed. Hands open and close several exterior pockets, then zip one.
beats.note: BEAT JOB: pocket stack. Volume of proof rather than depth.

beats.script: My favorite feature is the bottom compartment
beats.visual: CU, 4.0s, the longest hold in the ad. Green armchair. A woman leans in and unzips the bottom compartment, pulls out sandals.
beats.emotion: PEAK. The ad slows down here
beats.note: BEAT JOB: superlative pick. The only place the cutting relaxes. Announced as a favourite, not as a spec, which is why it reads as opinion rather than copy.

beats.script: Shoes go in there. Toiletries go in there.
beats.visual: MS. Bed. She packs shoes, then toiletries, into the bottom compartment and zips it.
beats.note: BEAT JOB: proof of the pick. A repetition beat, two short parallel sentences over two actions.

beats.script: The other thing I didn't expect to love this much?
beats.visual: MS. Room corner, wood floor, plant. Duffel on a white roller, static, nobody in frame.

notes.title: APPROVAL GATE
notes.text: Nothing renders, animates or generates until Brooks approves this board. Approve or redirect four things: the angle (VEL-A-002, the compromise trip bag), the script as written, the 20 scene structure, and the casting call in the next note.

notes.title: CASTING
notes.text: One creator, one woman, mid 40s, locked as the same reference in every shot she appears in. The reference ad used three different women and five colorways because it is stitched from affiliate footage. We do not copy that. Light Chocolate is the hero in every scene except the colorway spread and the handover.

notes.title: STRUCTURE
notes.text: One continuous voiceover across the full 85 seconds, never spliced per beat, and no talking head anywhere. The reference has no on-camera speech either, and that is the single most useful structural fact the watch turned up.

notes.title: WHAT WAS KEPT
notes.text: All 20 beat functions in their original order. The cut rhythm: 28 cuts, mean 3.0 seconds, nothing over 4 seconds, the two longest holds reserved for the superlative pick and the surprise payoff. The energy curve including the reflective dip at 3 to 9 seconds and the small intimate close. The shot grammar: hands-only macro for every claim, wide for every transport beat, product-alone statics as breath beats.

notes.title: SCRIPT FLOW PORTED
notes.text: The retrospective verdict opener, the concession and its resolution, the flat product naming, the permission line, the ordinal connective, the value aside dropped mid demo, the superlative announced as a favourite, the setup and payoff split across a cut, the And honestly pivot, unasked-for social proof, the offer stated once with no adjectives, and the personal gift close.

notes.title: WHAT WAS REBUILT
notes.text: Their claims ladder is bolt-on features: a trolley sleeve, a padded laptop pocket, a sealed shoe compartment, a personal-item fee dodge. Every rung is something a competitor could add next season. Ours is construction: no zipper anywhere, a one-piece flap that folds all the way back, a working gold turn post with two belt straps hooking over staple plates, rolled handles that only reach a forearm, no logo inside or out, holds its shape packed or empty.

notes.title: SWAP TEST
notes.text: Drop the reference's own bag into our script and it fails at the no-zipper line, the turn post, the fold-back flap, the forearm-only handles and the no-logo claim. Five of six construction lines break. The angle cannot be lifted by anyone else.

notes.title: SIX MONTH TEST
notes.text: No season, no holiday, no calendar beat anywhere in the script. Short trips and a long weekend are permanent categories. The only dated line is the offer, which swaps when the sale does.

notes.title: PRODUCT TRUTH, VERIFIED LIVE 2026-09-03
notes.text: The Eleanor Weekender, 209.99 struck to 159.99. Approx 18 inches wide by 14.5 high by 7 deep. Packs 2 to 3 day trips, fits the overhead bin, keeps its shape packed full or barely at all, working gold turn-lock, leather slip pocket, two year warranty. Colorways: Light Chocolate, Army Green, Dark Chocolate, and Black on pre-order for mid September 2026.

notes.title: OPEN CONFLICT FOR BROOKS
notes.text: The live product page describes the interior as natural cotton-canvas lining. The 8/08 footage of the physical bag shows a smooth caramel leather lining with a matching caramel slip pocket, and the product record already corrected that canvas description once as an error. The script sidesteps it by claiming only the leather slip pocket and never naming the lining material, but the product page copy should be fixed either way.

notes.title: PRODUCTION LAWS
notes.text: Real 4K product footage carries every beat where the hardware or the interior is large in frame. Never regenerate what was already filmed. No engine animates the bag being opened, unfastened, or carried while walking. No shoulder carry anywhere. Captions burn from the script, never from ASR, and the word Weekender never renders as engine text.

notes.title: ONLY REAL GENERATION RISK
notes.text: The overhead bin beat at 0:22. Three variants, pick clean, frame QA against the closed hero before anything animates. If all three fail, cut the beat and the ad runs about 83 seconds. Everything else is either real footage or a simple staged beat with no hand on the hardware.

Workflow: reference-adapt. Brand: velantra. Product: weekender (The Eleanor Weekender).

## Outcome

Complete. The reference resolved, downloaded and was watched frame by frame (28 beats,
81.15 seconds, 167 days running). It was autopsied as a strategist, redirected for our
product, scripted in prose, passed the law gate clean on the first run with
speaker=creator, logged in the tracker, and delivered as a two lane Cutroom storyboard
with 183 cards. No images, video or voice were generated, per the run flags.

Concept id: **VEL-WEEKENDER-ONEBAG-01**. Angle: **VEL-A-002, the compromise trip bag**.
Runtime about 85 seconds, 20 scenes, 28 cuts, one continuous voiceover.

The reference turned out to be structurally different from what its own label suggests.
It is tagged a UGC talking head, but nobody speaks on camera at any point. It is one
continuous voiceover laid over silent b-roll cut from at least 3 different women and 5
colorways, which is an affiliate montage artifact. Our version keeps the voiceover
structure and drops the three-women part: one creator, locked, in every shot.

The reference product is a soft synthetic duffel built around zippers, a trolley sleeve,
a padded laptop pocket and a sealed bottom compartment. Ours is a structured
leather-over-canvas bag with no zipper anywhere. Tracing was never an option, so the
redirect is the whole job: the beat functions, cut rhythm, energy curve and script flow
moves were kept exactly, and every claim in the ladder was rebuilt from our own
construction facts.

## Decisions and assumptions

**Live product truth beat the skill in three places.** The live page was fetched before
any claim was written.
1. Colorways are now four (Light Chocolate, Army Green, Dark Chocolate, and Black on
   pre-order for mid September 2026). The product skill records three.
2. The live page reads "Packs 2 to 3 day trips." The script says 3 days of clothes and
   goes no higher.
3. **Interior lining conflict, unresolved and flagged.** The live page says "Natural
   cotton-canvas lining with a leather slip pocket." Brooks's own 2026-08-08 footage of
   the physical bag shows a smooth caramel leather lining, and the product record notes
   that the cotton-canvas description was already caught and corrected once as an error.
   The live page wins by the workflow rule, but here the live page contradicts the
   physical object. Rather than assert either, the script claims only the leather slip
   pocket, which both sources agree on, and never names the lining material. The page
   copy should be corrected. This is on the board as an open conflict.

**No colorway count in the voiceover.** The fourth colorway is on pre-order, and the
house law requires a pre-order claim to carry a ship date. Naming a count would either
break that law or force a ship date into a creator's mouth. The count is dropped and
three shipping colorways appear on screen instead.

**Three reference claims could not be ported and were replaced, not softened.**
The personal-item and baggage-fee claim is false for an 18 inch wide bag and would become
a support ticket, so the overhead bin claim (live PDP copy) takes that slot. The padded
laptop pocket does not exist, so the beat shows a laptop going in flat against the leather
slip pocket, which keeps the demonstration and shrinks the claim to what is true. The
shoulder-carry relief line is impossible on our short rolled handles, so the forearm carry
with hands free takes that slot.

**The superlative slot was the load-bearing swap.** The reference reserves its longest
hold and its only slowdown for "my favorite feature is the bottom compartment." That slot
now carries the one-piece flap folding all the way back, which is the strongest fact we
own and the one thing on the board that no competitor can copy.

**Angle sourcing is honest about a gap.** There is no women's Weekender VoC in the folder.
VEL-A-002 rests on three real verbatims (the size objection and the slouch objection from
the 8/31 men's comment pull, the no-logo reward from the ICP), and the compromise-bag
framing on top of them is labelled [INFERRED] in the bank with its reasoning shown. It was
not promoted to a quote. A dr-voc-mining pass on women's weekender language is the next
research job and is recorded as the bank's biggest gap.

**One instruction conflict, resolved in favour of the workflow spec.** The dr-os pipeline
guide carries a mirror-fidelity law that says reference adaptations should trace the
reference. The workflow spec for this run says never trace and redirect instead. The
workflow spec governed. In this case the two would have collided regardless, because a
one-to-one copy of a zippered duffel is not producible with our bag.

**Runtime.** The reference runs 81.15 seconds at roughly 190 words per minute. Our script
is about 280 words, which lands near 85 seconds at the same pace. Cut count and rhythm
match the reference (28 cuts, mean 3.0 seconds against their 2.90, nothing over 4 seconds).

**Self-audit.** Swap test passes: the reference's own bag fails five of the six
construction lines. Six-month test passes: no season, no holiday, no calendar beat, and
the only dated line is the offer. Every claim has a demonstration beat on its own card.

personification, no invented spec, no Birkin or Hermes anywhere in script, prompts or
cards. Law gate clean on the script and on all three saved artifacts.
